_comment: doc 11 §2.15 (audio is doc 11's, Phase 2). The single tunables file for game/audio/: buses, the voice pool, every cue, the sim-event → cue rules, and the ambience beds. Nothing in game/audio/*.gd hardcodes a level, a cooldown or a distance (constitution §3): AudioEvents decides WHICH cue and WHEN from this file, AudioService only plays what it is handed. Streams resolve as `asset_root + <stream> + .wav`, all generated by tools/gen_audio.py.

mix._comment: `settings_key` is the ui/settings_model.gd row that scales the whole mix (data/ui.json.settings.rows: `sound_volume`, 0..1, default 0.8). At or below `silence_below_volume01` the Master bus is muted outright rather than played at -60 dB.

pool._comment: One AudioStreamPlayer per voice, allocated once at setup. `max_per_cue` is what stops a storm from spending the whole pool on thunder; stealing prefers the oldest voice of the lowest priority.

world._comment: Positional model. The listener is the camera (the shell passes it in). `tile_m` matches constitution §6. `speed_of_sound_ms` is what delays thunder behind its flash (doc 11 §2.15). `position_keys` maps a payload id to a locator kind so the shell's `Callable(kind, id) -> Vector3` can place an event that only carries an id.
world._curves: `inverse` is ref_m/d with a linear window fade to exactly 0 at max_m (so a far event is dropped, not mixed at -60 dB); `linear` is the window alone; `none` opts a cue out of distance entirely — the player's own confirmation and a critical sting are feedback, not scenery.

cues._comment: gain_db is the trim on top of the level already authored into the WAV. `pitch_jitter` is ± a fraction, drawn from the audio RNG stream, so a repeated cue never phases against itself. `duck` (0..1) pulls the ambience beds down while the cue lands.

events._comment: First matching rule wins (AlertsModel's rule shape, same reasons). `match` is exact equality, `range` is min/max on a number; both may read a derived field — `@distance_m` is the metres from the listener to the event, resolved before any rule is tried, which is what lets thunder pick crack-vs-rumble without a second concept. `dedup_by` is `cue` (all of them are one story: twelve dark blocks are ONE thunk) or `key` (each entity is its own). `cooldown_s` is measured from the last accepted request of that identity, not from playback, so a delayed cue still gates the next one.

Power. BlockDarkChanged is the sim's truth; render_blackout_started / render_relight_started are doc 11 §2.15's renderer hooks for the same beat. Both are mapped on purpose — they share a cue identity, so a shell that feeds both event sources still gets exactly one thunk per blackout.

Lightning. `speed_of_sound` turns the metres into the delay behind the flash; the near rule fires the crack, everything further away smears into the rumble. Both carry world_pos already, so no locator is involved.
Incidents. doc 08's notification class decides the sting: P1 critical gets the urgent one, everything else the routine one.

Dispatch. unit_dispatched carries no position, so the incident's tile — remembered from incident_created — places the siren; the pass-by fade is authored into the asset, and distance only sets its level.

beds._comment: Looping ambience. `source` names the computation in AudioEvents: `day`/`night` cross-fade on the shell's night01, `precip` follows weather_changed.precip01, `wind` maps wind_kph into 0..1, `sites` follows how many construction sites are live and how far the nearest one is. Each bed's gain is lerped over mix.bed_ramp_s and the player is stopped outright below mix.bed_stop_below, so a silent bed costs nothing.
